name: Observational astronomy under the Abbasid caliph al-Ma'mun
summary: Astronomers sponsored by caliph al-Ma'mun observed the Sun and Moon at Baghdad in 828 and near Damascus in 831 to 833, and new astronomical tables were made from the results.
description: Al-Ma'mun, who had Greek astronomical works including Ptolemy's translated into Arabic, sponsored two sets of observations. The first was made in 828 in the Shammasiyya quarter of Baghdad by astronomers including Yahya ibn Abi Mansur and al-Khwarizmi, around the solstices and equinoxes. The second was made under Khalid al-Marwarrudhi at Dayr Murran near Damascus between 831 and 833, and al-Ma'mun ordered astronomical tables to be prepared from it.

impact.note: A court programme whose results served astronomers across the Islamic world (reach 1); it re-measured known solar and lunar quantities and did not create a new capability (depth 1); the source credits it with inspiring the observatory as an institution and royal patronage of astronomy (generativity 2).

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: The first set of observations sponsored by al-Ma'mun was made in the Shammasiyya area of Baghdad in 828.

evidence.supports: first was done in Baghdad, in 828, in the Shammāsiyya area, by astronomers

date.basis: As the cited source gives it.

events.statement: A second set of observations was made in two periods between 831 and 833; the source places it at Dayr Murran, on a hill near Damascus.

evidence.supports: observations, done in two periods between 831 and 833, lasted more than a year
evidence.locator: Entry on Ma'mun, p. 733; the preceding sentences give the place and the observer

earliest_record.rationale: The earliest dated evidence found for this capability in this community. No review has yet confirmed that nothing earlier exists.

unresolved.note: Date the translations of the Sindhind and the Almagest and show what they were used for.
Decide whether the wider Abbasid tradition of zij tables (c. 770 to 930) needs its own record; the dataset already holds the Tusi couple of 1245 (tusi-couple-lunar-model-1245).
Settle the exact years of the Baghdad observations, which other sources give as 828 to 829 or 829 to 830.

research.note: The source says that under al-Ma'mun Greek astronomical works, including all of Ptolemy's, were translated into Arabic, and that the resulting tables must have used earlier material for the planets; the observations built on that received astronomy.
